propositions.text: Seeks refugee protection under section 96 and subsection 97(1) of IRPA
propositions.quote: XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX seeks refugee protection pursuant to section 96 and subsection 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).1

paragraphs.summary: The applicant seeks refugee protection under section 96 and subsection 97(1) of IRPA.

propositions.text: Claimant appeared without counsel; former counsel withdrew July 6, 2010
propositions.quote: The claimant appeared without counsel. The panel noted that the claimant's former counsel of record withdrew his services on July 6, 2010.

propositions.text: Requested 30-day adjournment to retain new counsel
propositions.quote: The claimant sought an adjournment of 30 days in order to retain and instruct new counsel.

propositions.text: Panel inquired about efforts to obtain counsel since July 6, 2010
propositions.quote: The panel inquired as to what efforts the claimant had undertaken to obtain and instruct counsel since July 6, 2010.

propositions.text: Claimant spoke to two lawyers but neither agreed to represent him
propositions.quote: The claimant replied that he had spoken to two lawyers, but could not remember their full names, neither of whom agreed to represent him.

propositions.text: Panel considered Rule 48(4) factors in adjournment request
propositions.quote: In considering the request for the adjournment, the panel took into account all the factors set out in Rule 48(4).2

propositions.text: Claimant had over two years to prepare and over two months to get new counsel
propositions.quote: The panel noted that the claimant had more than two years to prepare for the hearing. The claimant had more than two months to obtain and instruct new counsel in advance of the present hearing.

propositions.text: Claimant did not demonstrate serious effort to be ready to start hearing
propositions.quote: The claimant, in approaching only two other lawyers, did not demonstrate serious effort to be ready to start the hearing.

propositions.text: Allowing adjournment would unreasonably delay proceedings; request denied
propositions.quote: The panel determined that allowing the application would unreasonably delay the proceedings in all the circumstances of the present case. The panel therefore denied the request for a postponement.

propositions.text: Claimant indicated willingness to proceed without counsel if adjournment denied
propositions.quote: The claimant indicated that he would proceed without counsel if the request for postponement were not granted.

propositions.text: Panel confirmed claimant was ready to proceed; claimant affirmed readiness
propositions.quote: After denying the request, the panel confirmed with the claimant that he was ready to proceed and the claimant replied in the affirmative.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found the claimant appeared without counsel, denied a 30-day adjournment request due to insufficient effort and delay concerns, and confirmed claimant's readiness to proceed.

propositions.text: Claimant granted asylum in USA in 2000 as Rwandan national
propositions.quote: The claimant was granted asylum in the USA in XXXXX 2000 on the basis of his alleged Rwandan nationality.

propositions.text: Obtained US permanent resident status in 2005 on same basis
propositions.quote: He obtained permanent resident status in the USA on that same basis in 2005.

propositions.text: US DHS served notice to cancel asylum status in 2008 due to belief claimant was Ugandan national
propositions.quote: In 2008, the US Department of Homeland Security served notice on the claimant to cancel his asylum status, because they had information that led them to believe he was in fact a national of the Republic of Uganda.

propositions.text: Claimant requested 90-day delay to gather evidence; hearing nothing, visited Canada
propositions.quote: The claimant received the notice to appear for this proceeding and requested a delay of 90 days for the purpose of gathering evidence. Hearing nothing from the US authorities, he decided to visit a friend in Canada.

propositions.text: Learned asylum status cancelled after failing to appear; received deportation hearing notice
propositions.quote: Subsequent to his arrival, he learned that his asylum status had been cancelled when he failed to appear as convoked. He also received a copy of a notice to appear for a deportation hearing in the USA.

propositions.text: Claimant alleges prior Rwandan nationality declarations were misrepresentations
propositions.quote: The claimant alleges that his previous declarations of Rwandan nationality were misrepresentations.

propositions.text: Claimant alleges detention in Uganda in 1999 due to acquaintance with opponent of government
propositions.quote: The claimant now alleges that, in 1999, he was detained on two occasions by the security services of Uganda, because of his acquaintance with a XXXX in the Ugandan armed forces suspected of being an opponent of the government.

propositions.text: Entered USA in 1999 on non-immigrant visa; applied for asylum in 2000
propositions.quote: He subsequently obtained a US non-immigrant visa and entered the USA in XXXXXX 1999, and applied for asylum in the USA in XXXX, 2000.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges prior Rwandan nationality was misrepresented; he was detained in Uganda in 1999, entered USA on visa, applied for asylum in 2000, and later faced asylum cancellation.

propositions.text: Minister served notice of intention to intervene by documents
propositions.quote: The Minister of Public Safety served notice of his intention to intervene in the present hearing by way of documents.

propositions.text: Minister's intervention related to claimant's credibility assessment based on US DHS information
propositions.quote: The Minister's intervention related to the assessment of the credibility of the claimant, in light of information received from the US Department of Homeland Security.

paragraphs.summary: The respondent served notice to intervene regarding the claimant's credibility based on US DHS information.

propositions.text: Exclusion issue included in hearing screening form dated April 22, 2010
propositions.quote: it was included as an issue to be raised at the hearing in the screening form dated April 22, 2010.

propositions.text: Panel satisfied claimant had adequate notice exclusion issue would be raised
propositions.quote: The panel is satisfied that the claimant had adequate notice that this issue would be raised in the present hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found the claimant had adequate notice that exclusion would be raised at the hearing.

propositions.text: Determines claimant has US permanent resident status and is excluded from refugee protection
propositions.quote: The panel determines, on a balance of probabilities, that the claimant has permanent resident status in the USA and is therefore excluded from Refugee Protection.

propositions.text: Alternatively, claimant is neither Convention refugee nor person in need of protection
propositions.quote: In the alternative, the panel determines that the claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of Canada's protection.

propositions.text: Determinative issues were claimant's identity and credibility
propositions.quote: In arriving at the decision on inclusion, the determinative issues were the identity and credibility of the claimant.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker determined claimant is excluded due to US permanent resident status or alternatively not a refugee or person in need of protection, focusing on identity and credibility.

propositions.text: Schedule to IRPA provides relevant provisions
propositions.quote: The Schedule to the IRPA provides in part as follows:

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker notes the Schedule to IRPA provides relevant provisions.

propositions.text: Article 1E excludes persons recognized as having nationality rights in country of residence
propositions.quote: E. This Convention shall not apply to a person who is recognized by the competent authorities of the country in which he has taken residence as having the rights and obligations which are attached to the possession of the nationality of that country.

paragraphs.summary: Article 1E of the Convention excludes persons recognized as having nationality rights in their country of residence.

propositions.text: Documents seized included US Refugee Travel Document and permanent resident card
propositions.quote: Among the documents seized by the Immigration Officer were a US Refugee Travel Document, identifying the bearer as enjoying permanent resident status in the USA, and a US permanent resident card.

propositions.text: Claimant testified documents were genuine and presented them at Pearson Airport in 2008
propositions.quote: The claimant testified that they were both genuine documents and that he had presented them both when he was granted admission as a temporary resident at Pearson Airport on XXXX, 2008.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found seized documents showed US permanent resident status, which claimant testified were genuine and presented at admission.

propositions.text: Valid permanent resident status in USA triggers Article 1E exclusion
propositions.quote: The panel determines that valid and subsisting permanent resident status in the USA engages section 1E of the Convention.

propositions.text: Permanent resident card creates rebuttable presumption of status
propositions.quote: The possession of a permanent resident card creates a rebuttable presumption that the claimant enjoys that status.

propositions.text: Claimant's asylum terminated in 2008 but permanent resident status not addressed
propositions.quote: It is clear from the documentation before the panel that the claimant's grant of asylum was terminated, effective XXXX, 2008. This notice did not however address the permanent resident status which followed the initial grant of asylum, some five years later.

propositions.text: Claimant felt he lost permanent resident status in 2008
propositions.quote: The claimant testified that he felt he no longer had permanent resident status as of XXXX, 2008.

propositions.text: Panel disagrees; claimant remains permanent resident until deportation order issued
propositions.quote: With respect, the panel does not agree. The claimant himself introduced a notice to appear for a deportation hearing scheduled for XXXX, 2008. The panel is satisfied that the claimant enjoys permanent resident status in the USA until the competent authority issues a deportation order against him.

propositions.text: Claimant chose not to appear at deportation hearing fearing removal
propositions.quote: The claimant declared that he chose not to appear for the deportation hearing because he feared subsequent removal from the USA.

propositions.text: US DHS disclosure states claimant failed to appear for termination interview; asylum terminated; no info on further action
propositions.quote: The individual failed to appear for his termination interview; thereafter his asylum status was terminated. The Asylum Office issued a Notice to Appear (NTA), but there was no information to indicate if any further action was taken.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found claimant's valid US permanent resident status triggers exclusion; claimant's asylum ended but permanent resident status continues until deportation order.

propositions.text: Minister's disclosure confirms claimant subject to deportation hearing
propositions.quote: The Minister's disclosure confirms the claimant's own evidence that he was the subject of a separate deportation hearing.

propositions.text: Panel finds no record of deportation order issued against claimant
propositions.quote: The panel finds it reasonable to believe that if a deportation order had been made against the claimant at the June 16 hearing, or subsequently, the US authorities would have a record of that deportation and have disclosed it.

propositions.text: Claimant has no evidence of deportation order
propositions.quote: The panel asked the claimant if he had any evidence that a deportation order had been issued to him and he replied that he had no such evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found no evidence of a deportation order against claimant despite deportation hearing, and claimant has no such evidence.

propositions.text: On balance of probabilities, claimant remains US permanent resident
propositions.quote: After considering the whole of the documentary evidence before the panel and the claimant's testimony, the panel is satisfied that he is today still a permanent resident of the USA, on a balance of probabilities.

propositions.text: Claimant excluded from refugee protection under Article 1E and s. 98 IRPA
propositions.quote: He is therefore subject to Article 1E of the Convention and excluded from refugee protection pursuant to s. 98 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker concludes claimant remains US permanent resident and is excluded from refugee protection under Article 1E and s. 98 IRPA.

propositions.text: At hearing, claimant declined to affirm contents of Personal Information Form (PIF)
propositions.quote: At the outset of the hearing, when the claimant was asked to affirm the contents of his Personal Information Form (PIF), the claimant declined to do so and testified that the PIF misrepresented the facts.

propositions.text: Claimant admitted signature on PIF and understood it was equivalent to oath
propositions.quote: The panel asked the claimant if he had signed the PIF at page 13, and he testified that it was his signature. The panel asked the claimant if he understood that the signature was equivalent to giving evidence under oath, and he replied that he understood this.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found claimant declined to affirm PIF contents but admitted signature and understood it was under oath.

propositions.text: PIF contained multiple untruthful items including birthplace, nationality, family, education, arrest, residence, passport, and narrative
propositions.quote: The panel proceeded to review the items in the PIF which were untruthful. They included the following items: * the claimant's place of birth; * the claimant's nationality, ethnicity and mother tongue; * the details of the claimant's marital status and family members; * the details of his alleged education and employment in Rwanda; * the alleged arrest by the government of Rwanda; * the details of his alleged residence in Rwanda; * the allegation that his Ugandan passport was improperly obtained; * the whole of his narrative.

propositions.text: Claimant said he assumed false Rwandan identity to improve asylum chances in USA
propositions.quote: The claimant replied that he physically resembles a Rwandan ethnic Tutsi, and that he felt by assuming this nationality he would stand a greater chance of receiving asylum in the USA.

propositions.text: Claimant maintained false identity through US permanent residence and refugee travel document
propositions.quote: He elected to continue maintaining that false identity through his application for permanent residence in the USA, his application for a US refugee travel document, and three years of living in that country as a permanent residence.

propositions.text: Claimant testified he resolved to be truthful in Canada but maintained false identity in Canadian applications until Minister's disclosure
propositions.quote: The claimant testified that he resolved to be truthful in Canada. However, the panel notes that in both his application for protection made to the immigration officer and his PIF, he maintained his false identity. His change of heart appears to have come about only subsequent to the disclosure of the Minister of June 23, 2010.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found claimant's PIF had many untruthful items; claimant admitted assuming false Rwandan identity to improve asylum chances and maintained it until Minister's disclosure.

propositions.text: Panel asked claimant for evidence corroborating Ugandan identity and persecution; claimant had none
propositions.quote: The panel asked the claimant if he had any evidence to corroborate his alleged identity as a citizen of Uganda, and the alleged persecution he suffered in that country and he replied that he did not.

propositions.text: Only evidence on core issues is claimant's uncorroborated testimony
propositions.quote: The only evidence on these core issues is the claimant's uncorroborated testimony.

propositions.text: Claimant's history of misrepresentation reduces weight given to his testimony
propositions.quote: However, the claimant has demonstrated a significant willingness to misrepresent his identity to officials in both Canada and the USA over a period of eleven years. In the circumstances, the panel gives little weight to the claimant's testimony about his identity and the alleged events in Uganda.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found claimant had no corroborating evidence and gave little weight to his testimony due to history of misrepresentation.

propositions.text: Claimant must establish identity on balance of probabilities (Yip)
propositions.quote: In the Yip decision, the Federal Court held that the claimant has the fundamental obligation to establish his or her identity on a balance of probabilities.

propositions.text: Claimant must bring all evidence believed necessary to prove claim (Kante)
propositions.quote: In the Kante decision, the Court affirmed that the claimant must come to a hearing with all of the evidence that he or she is able to offer and believes is necessary to prove the claim.

propositions.text: Claimant introduced no evidence to prove personal identity or Ugandan nationality
propositions.quote: The claimant introduced no evidence to prove his personal identity or his nationality of Uganda.

propositions.text: Rule 7 requires claimant to document identity and claim elements
propositions.quote: Rule 7 requires the claimant to document his identity and other elements of his claim.

propositions.text: Claimant has not discharged burden regarding new identity and nationality; true identity unknown
propositions.quote: With respect to his newly declared identity and Ugandan nationality the panel finds the claimant has not discharged this burden. The panel does not know who the claimant truly is.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker cited case law and rules requiring claimant to prove identity, found claimant failed to do so, and true identity remains unknown.

propositions.text: S. 106 IRPA requires considering documentation and explanations regarding identity credibility
propositions.quote: S. 106 of IRPA requires the panel to take into the account, with respect to the credibility of a claimant, whether the claimant possesses acceptable documentation establishing identity, and, if not, whether they have provided a reasonable explanation for the lack of documentation or have taken reasonable steps to obtain the documentation.

propositions.text: Claimant failed to satisfy s. 106 obligations; negative credibility inference drawn
propositions.quote: In light of the analysis above, the panel finds that the claimant has not satisfied this statutory obligation and draws a negative inference on his credibility as a result.

propositions.text: Without knowing true identity, panel not satisfied claimant faces serious persecution risk; not a Convention refugee
propositions.quote: Without knowing his true identity, the panel cannot be satisfied that the claimant faces a serious possibility of persecution on Convention grounds. He is not a Convention refugee, accordingly.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found claimant failed s. 106 IRPA obligations, drew negative credibility inference, and concluded claimant is not a Convention refugee.

propositions.text: Insufficient reliable evidence claimant faces danger of torture or risk to life or cruel treatment
propositions.quote: There is not sufficient, reliable evidence before the panel to suggest that the claimant faces a danger of torture or that, on a balance of probabilities, he faces a risk to his life or to cruel and unusual treatment or punishment.

propositions.text: Claimant is not a person in need of protection
propositions.quote: He is not a person in need of protection, accordingly.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found insufficient evidence of danger or risk and concluded claimant is not a person in need of protection.

propositions.text: Claimant excluded from refugee protection under s. 98 IRPA
propositions.quote: The panel determines that the claimant is excluded from refugee protection pursuant to s. 98 of the IRPA.

propositions.text: Alternatively, claimant is neither Convention refugee nor person in need of protection; claim rejected
propositions.quote: In the alternative, the panel determines that the claimant is neither a Convention refugee, nor a person in need of protection and therefore rejects his claim.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker excluded claimant from refugee protection or alternatively rejected claim as not refugee or person in need of protection.
